newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle slip $1 at $66 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle slip $1 at $66 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $66.00 per cwt, down $1.00 from Wednesday, but sales volume was said to be too light for an adequate market test, feedlot sources said.

About 200 to 400 steers and heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area. The sales brought weekly movement near 64,000 head, including 13,700 formulated and 1,300 contracted cattle to be shipped this week.
About 1,500 head sold in Kansas, but the quality was below the cattle that sold Wednesday at $67.00, the sources said.
Week to date sales in Kansas totaled 65,300 head including 16,600 or about 26 percent previously contracted or formulated cattle, USDA reported.
Further bids at $66.00 were passed by owners asking $67.00 for the remainder of cattle, feedlot sources said.
Although sales were brisk on Wednesday, cattle still remained on this week's estimated showlists, they said.
Packers reportedly bought less cattle than expected because they augmented fed cattle supplies with contract cattle that became available this week, the sources said.
